lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: # caddy-8015: httpcaddyfile: new `tls_automate_names` global option

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: PR #8015 closes issue #7122. It adds one Caddyfile global option and five adapt fixtures. One review comment and one conversation comment each asked for a change, and each added one fixture. The final name came from a naming thread in the conversation comments.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Story

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Title: the PR title, or a plain line about a global option that manages certificates for names without serving them.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Why: present, from issue #7122. The issue asks for a Caddyfile way to automate a certificate without an HTTPS site, for a wildcard with no site block and for names that only a layer 4 app serves.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Size: small. The Go change is about 100 lines in two files. The five fixtures are long JSON, but each pins one case.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Parts: 0 or 1. One story.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Groups: 1 or 2. The fixtures sit with the code, or in one trailing group.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Groups

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 1. Option and tls app: `caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/options.go` and `caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go`. `parseOptAutomateNames` fills the name list, and `buildTLSApp` reads it to write the `automate` loader and the automation policies.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 2. Adapt fixtures: the five `caddytest/integration/caddyfile_adapt/tls_automate_names*.caddyfiletest` files. They are generated adapt outputs that pin one case each: the issue scenario, no site blocks, internal names with a repeated option, a name with its own site policy, and `auto_https off`. They can also sit in group 1.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Must

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Each name in `tls_automate_names` goes into the tls app `automate` loader, so Caddy manages its certificate with no site block and no HTTP route for that name.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Public names with no policy of their own get a new automation policy only when a global automation or ACME option such as `email` is set, because the catch-all policy is dropped and without their own policy the names miss the global issuer.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - A listed name that is already a subject of an automation policy keeps that policy and stays in the `automate` loader, because a second policy for the same subject fails the adapt, as the review comment asked.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - The `tls_automate_names` block is not gated on `auto_https off` or `disable_certs`, unlike the hostless-key block above it, so a listed name is still managed when `auto_https` is off.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Good

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - All five fixtures match the code at head, and two of them (`tls_automate_names_without_site_block` and `tls_automate_names_auto_https_off`) hold only the `automate` loader and no automation policy, because they set no global option.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - In `tls_automate_names.caddyfiletest`, the new policy for `*.example.com` gets the same issuers as the `foo.example.com` site policy, so `consolidateAutomationPolicies` folds both into one policy.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Repeating the option appends to the list, because `parseOptAutomateNames` appends to the `existing` value, and `tls_automate_names_internal.caddyfiletest` pins it with `second.example.com`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Names that cannot get a public certificate, such as `localhost` and `192.168.1.5`, go into `internalAP` and get the internal issuer, the same as a site block gives them.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `hasGlobalACMEDefaults` is a pure extraction of the old inline check in `buildTLSApp`, and unlike the check inside `newBaseAutomationPolicy` it counts `email`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - The PR body lists three adapt tests, but head has five, because the `existing_policy` and `auto_https_off` fixtures came after review.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Must not

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not put `options.go` and `tlsapp.go` in different groups, because the parser only fills the list that the tls app reads.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not make one group per fixture or spread the fixtures across groups.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not state that the PR adds three adapt tests, because head has five.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not ask for documentation in this diff, because the docs live in caddyserver/website#570, outside this repo.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not state that `auto_https off` stops Caddy from managing the listed names.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Notes

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The fixture check is `Good`: it needs each JSON output traced against `buildTLSApp`, including the issuer fill-in and the consolidation further down the function. Past runs missed it in 22 of 23 runs. The `auto_https off` claim is `Must`: the fixture shows `"automatic_https": {"disable": true}` next to the `automate` loader, and the conversation comment says the override is deliberate. Past runs often left it out of `lookFor`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The PR body says a name with a site block "stays listed here". That is true at head: the name stays in the loader, and only the extra policy is skipped.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: `parts` allows 0 or 1, since one story may or may not get a named part. `groups` allows 1 to 3 around the 2 group estimate. `size` allows small or medium, since the fixture JSON can read as more work than it is. `mechanicalPaths` holds the five fixtures, so one group holds all of them. `together` holds the two Go files. No `apart`: with one story, no pair of paths must stay apart.
